prompts.title: Recent form of Espanyol
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 scene, roughly 8 seconds, split into an upper two-thirds visual zone and a permanent lower quarter reserved for yellow subtitles in Spanish (lime #c5ed74 on GoatLab charcoal #101412).

EDITORIAL VARIANT (kinetic typography): the Spanish heading "RENDIMIENTO RECIENTE" slides up from behind a charcoal mask, then three oversized words cycle on a rhythmic beat — "VICTORIAS", "EMPATES", "DERROTAS" — each punching in with a scale from 1.15 to 1.0, warm white #edf0e6 fill, lime accent underline, slate #8ca6bf shadow offset. A thin lime tick marks each beat. No axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Layout: heading at the top fifth, kinetic word stack centred, a small crest-slot on the left edge. Camera: subtle push-in during the word cycle, then a slow settle. Exit is a vertical wipe upward.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (grouped count bars): same charcoal field, Spanish title "FORMA EN LOS ÚLTIMOS PARTIDOS" top-aligned. A single grouped bar chart sits in the middle half of the frame with one shared zero baseline running horizontally: three groups labelled in Spanish — "Victorias" {{home.wins}}, "Empates" {{home.draws}}, "Derrotas" {{home.losses}} — all in unit "partidos". Bars in lime for wins, slate for draws, warm white outline for losses, all sharing one count scale anchored at zero so unequal magnitudes stay comparable. Direct value labels sit above each bar in warm white, with the unit "partidos" shown once on the vertical axis title. Sample annotation pinned to the baseline: "Muestra: {{home.n}} partidos" and "Fuente: Bzzoiro", both in Spanish, in small slate type. Bars grow upward from zero over three sequential beats, values counting up as they rise; the largest bar receives one lime flash of emphasis before everything returns to neutral. Camera holds steady with a very slight downward tilt toward the source line. Transition in: a lime rule that expands from centre; transition out: hard cut to charcoal. Both variants share the same subtitle band, framing and timing so the transition between them reads as one continuous 9:16 shot.

prompts.title: Goals for and against
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 scene, about 9 seconds, with the lower quarter held permanently for yellow Spanish subtitles (lime #c5ed74 on charcoal #101412).

EDITORIAL VARIANT (illustrative pitch and ball path): a stylised half-pitch is drawn in slate #8ca6bf hairlines over charcoal, with a lime centre circle and penalty arc. The Spanish heading "GOLES" sits large at the top in warm white #edf0e6. A simplified ball travels along a curved lime path from the left flank into the net, then a second path in slate returns across the pitch, giving an abstract sense of attacking and conceding without depicting any real match event. Player-crests are geometric blocks, not portraits. Composition keeps the ball path as the single focal point in the middle half; the pitch lines are secondary. Camera: gentle parallax drift as the ball arcs. Transition in: pitch lines sketch on in half a second; transition out: the ball exits frame right and the field wipes to charcoal.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (paired bars): Spanish title "GOLES A FAVOR Y EN CONTRA" top-aligned. A paired horizontal bar chart occupies the middle half: one row "Goles a favor" {{home.gf}} in lime, one row "Goles recibidos" {{home.ga}} in slate, both unit "goles", both measured on one shared scale starting at zero so the pair is directly comparable. Spanish axis label "Goles" sits at the scale end; value labels ride at each bar tip in warm white. Football context is carried by a small lime ball glyph beside the chart title, not by axes. Sample annotation directly under the chart: "Muestra: {{home.n}} partidos · Fuente: Bzzoira" written exactly as "Fuente: Bzzoiro" plus "partidos" unit, both in Spanish, in slate small type. Bars extend left-to-right on a staggered two-beat entry, values counting up, then one lime emphasis flash on the longer bar. Camera static with a micro push-in on the emphasis beat. Transition in: a lime ball rolls across the top edge; transition out: cross-fade to charcoal. Both variants share the same 9:16 framing, top heading and subtitle band.

prompts.title: Historical head-to-head duel
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 scene, about 10 seconds, lower quarter reserved throughout for yellow Spanish subtitles (lime #c5ed74 on charcoal #101412).

EDITORIAL VARIANT (visual duel): the frame is split down the middle by a vertical lime seam. Left half holds a warm white #edf0e6 shield block labelled "ESPANYOL" in Spanish; right half a slate #8ca6bf block labelled "ATLÉTICO". Both slide in from opposite edges and collide at the seam with a short shake, then hold in tension. Behind them, faint diagonal stripes in charcoal give depth. The Spanish heading "DUelo HISTÓRICO" — rendered as "DUELO HISTÓRICO" — sits top-centre in warm white with a lime underline. No axes, no counts, no sample claims: the duel is purely editorial. Camera: slow push-in toward the seam, then a subtle pull-back. Transition in: the seam draws itself top to bottom; transition out: both blocks retract outward leaving charcoal.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (historical counts): Spanish title "CRUCES PREVIOS" at the top, with a stacked count bar running across the middle of the frame on a single shared zero baseline and one common scale in unit "partidos": segments labelled in Spanish — "Espanyol" {{h2h.homeWins}}, "Empates" {{h2h.draws}}, "Atlético" {{h2h.awayWins}} — coloured lime, warm white outline and slate respectively, and the total shown as "Total de cruces: {{h2h.total}} partidos". Value labels sit inside or directly above each segment in warm white. Sample annotation attached permanently below the bar: "Muestra: {{h2h.total}} partidos · Fuente: Bzzoiro" in Spanish slate small type, with a one-line Spanish caveat "Datos históricos, no pronóstico". The bar fills left-to-right in one continuous motion over two beats, segment labels fading in as each fills; the largest segment gets a single lime emphasis flash. Camera holds, with a slight horizontal drift following the fill. Transition in: lime rule expands from centre; transition out: hard cut. Both variants share identical 9:16 framing, heading position and subtitle band.

prompts.title: History against current form
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 scene, roughly 10 seconds, with the lower quarter permanently occupied by yellow Spanish subtitles (lime #c5ed74 on charcoal #101412).

EDITORIAL VARIANT (team reveals and narrative emphasis): the Spanish narrative heading appears in two staged reveals, first "LA HISTORIA" in warm white #edf0e6, then, on the next beat, "FRENTE A LA FORMA" in lime #c5ed74, stacked top-aligned with a slate #8ca6bf hairline between them. Beneath, two abstract team blocks reveal from behind vertical masks — a lime block rising for Espanyol, a slate block rising for Atlético — and settle into a diagonal standoff with a thin charcoal gap between them. No axes, no counts, no sample claims in this variant. A single lime flare marks the second heading line as the focal point. Camera: slow push-in during the reveals, then a held frame. Transition in: heading lines wipe in from the left; transition out: blocks slide down and the frame clears to charcoal.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (grounded tension): Spanish title "CRUCES PREVIOS VS. FORMA ACTUAL" at the top. Two small chart panels share the middle half of the frame, each with its own zero baseline but clearly separated so units are not conflated. Upper panel: a single count bar for historical away wins, "Atlético en cruces" {{h2h.awayWins}} partidos, scale annotated "Muestra: {{h2h.total}} partidos". Lower panel: a single count bar for current wins, "Espanyol · victorias" {{home.wins}} partidos, scale annotated "Muestra: {{home.n}} partidos". Each panel carries its own Spanish source line — "Fuente: Bzzoiro" — directly under its bar, and a Spanish note "Muestras distintas: recuentos no comparables entre sí". Because the two panels use different samples, they are never placed on one shared axis. Bars grow upward from zero in a staggered two-beat entry with values counting up; emphasis is a single lime flash on the historical bar, the sole focal point. Camera static, tiny push-in on the emphasis beat. Transition in: lime rule expands from centre; transition out: cross-fade to charcoal. Both variants share the same 9:16 framing, heading stack and subtitle band.
